questions.question: Why must a method be marked mutating to change a property?

answers.text: So Swift knows which methods change the value, and can stop them being called on a let
Because methods cannot see properties otherwise

questions.why: mutating is a promise Swift checks: constants can only use non-mutating methods.

questions.question: After var b = a; b.score = 10, where a is a struct, what is a.score?

answers.text: Whatever it was before: b is a separate copy

questions.why: Structs are value types. Assigning one copies it.

questions.question: What is a computed property?

answers.text: A property whose value is worked out from other values each time it is read
A property that can only be set once
A property shared by every instance

questions.why: Computed properties store nothing; they calculate.

questions.question: What does init? mean?

answers.text: An initializer that can be skipped
An initializer that can fail and give nil

questions.why: A failable initializer returns an optional instance.

questions.question: How do you use a static let shared on a type Settings?
questions.why: Static members belong to the type, so you reach them through the type's name.
